interactions.label: Why are submucosal fibroids the type most commonly associated with menorrhagia?

params.question: Why are submucosal fibroids the type most commonly associated with menorrhagia?

answers.text: They compress adjacent pelvic organs, causing referred uterine bleeding

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Compression of adjacent organs (bladder, rectum) causes pressure symptoms such as urinary frequency — not menorrhagia.

answers.text: They distort the endometrial cavity and impair uterine contractility, enlarging the bleeding surface area

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Submucosal fibroids project into the endometrial cavity, distorting it and impairing the myometrium's ability to contract and compress bleeding vessels, while increasing the endometrial surface area.

answers.text: They undergo rapid growth and outstrip their blood supply, causing necrotic bleeding

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Necrotic (red) degeneration is an acute complication typically seen in pregnancy, not the mechanism of chronic menorrhagia from fibroids.

answers.text: They secrete excess oestrogen directly into the uterine cavity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Fibroids are oestrogen-dependent tumours but do not secrete oestrogen. They grow in response to circulating oestrogen rather than producing it.

overallFeedback.feedback: Submucosal fibroids project into the endometrial cavity, distorting it and preventing the myometrium from contracting effectively to stop bleeding — this enlarges the surface area and is the primary mechanism of menorrhagia.
Correct! Submucosal fibroids cause menorrhagia by distorting the endometrial cavity and impairing uterine contractility — this is why they cause the heaviest bleeding among all fibroid types.

params.question: Which symptom is the hallmark complaint that most specifically suggests uterine prolapse?

answers.text: Stress urinary incontinence on coughing or sneezing

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Stress incontinence occurs due to the associated cystocele (anterior wall descent) but is not specific to prolapse — it can occur independently without uterine descent.

answers.text: A sensation of something coming down per vaginum, worsening on standing and relieved by lying supine

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This positional variation — worsening on prolonged standing, straining, or coughing, and improving supine — reflects the effect of gravity on the descended uterus and is the hallmark of prolapse.

answers.text: Chronic constipation with the need to digitally assist defaecation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Digitation and incomplete rectal evacuation suggest a rectocele (posterior vaginal wall descent), which may accompany prolapse but is not its hallmark symptom.

answers.text: Dragging lower abdominal pain that worsens cyclically before menstruation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Cyclical premenstrual pain worsening with each cycle is characteristic of endometriosis, not uterine prolapse.

overallFeedback.feedback: The hallmark of uterine prolapse is a sensation of something coming down per vaginum that worsens on standing, straining, or coughing, and is relieved by lying supine — reflecting the descent of the uterus under gravity.
Correct! The sensation of something coming down — aggravated by standing and straining, relieved by lying down — is the hallmark of uterine prolapse.

params.question: A 60-year-old woman reports a single episode of light spotting on toilet paper, 3 years after her last menstrual period. She is otherwise well. What is the most appropriate next step?

answers.text: Reassure her that a single episode of light spotting is unlikely to be clinically significant

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Any vaginal bleeding ≥12 months after the last menstrual period is post-menopausal bleeding — an absolute alarm symptom. Reassurance without investigation risks missing endometrial carcinoma.

answers.text: Prescribe tranexamic acid and schedule a routine follow-up in 3 months

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Haemostatic agents address bleeding symptoms but do not investigate the cause. PMB requires urgent evaluation to exclude malignancy before any symptomatic treatment.

answers.text: Investigate urgently, as the amount of post-menopausal bleeding does not predict the severity of pathology

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: PMB mandates urgent investigation (transvaginal ultrasound ± endometrial sampling) regardless of bleeding amount — even a tiny spot can signify endometrial carcinoma.

answers.text: Start low-dose hormone replacement therapy to stabilise the atrophic endometrium

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: HRT is not the first response to PMB. The priority is to exclude malignancy through urgent investigation before considering any hormonal treatment.

overallFeedback.feedback: Post-menopausal bleeding is an absolute gynaecological alarm symptom. The amount of bleeding does not correlate with the severity of pathology — even light spotting requires urgent investigation to rule out endometrial carcinoma.
Correct! Post-menopausal bleeding — however slight — is an absolute alarm symptom that mandates urgent investigation to exclude endometrial malignancy.
